questions.q: Why write a pre-analysis plan before looking at any outcome data?
options: It makes the analysis run faster
It guarantees a significant result
It replaces the need for a control group
It fixes the metric, tests, and decision rule in advance so you cannot unconsciously pick whichever result looks best
questions.explain: Committing to the primary metric, alpha, and correction before seeing outcomes protects against metric-fishing and inflated false positives.

questions.q: The capstone tests two outcomes (churn and spend) at alpha 0.05. What does the plan require to claim a win with a Bonferroni correction?
options: p below 0.025 for each outcome
p below 0.10
p below 0.05 for at least one outcome
No correction is needed
questions.explain: Bonferroni divides alpha by the number of tests: 0.05 divided by 2 is 0.025.

questions.q: In the first look, spend has a mean of 46.82 and a median of 36.22, with skewness 2.61. What does this suggest?
options: The data has an error
Spend is right-skewed, so pair the mean comparison with a bootstrap interval and consider the median
Spend is normally distributed
The groups are unbalanced
questions.explain: A mean well above the median and a large positive skew signal a long right tail. Means can be distorted by extreme values, so a bootstrap interval and a median check add robustness.

questions.q: Why is the randomization and balance check done BEFORE testing the outcomes?
options: Because outcomes cannot be computed otherwise
Because balance guarantees a significant effect
Because if the split or groups look wrong, the outcome comparison may not be trustworthy
Because the p-value depends on it
questions.explain: A sample ratio mismatch or big group differences would point to an assignment or data problem that must be fixed before interpreting effects.

questions.q: Which set best describes what you should produce by the end of the capstone?
options: Only a p-value
A reproducible script, a results table, and a short written summary with a recommendation and its limitations
Only a chart
A machine learning model
questions.explain: A reproducible script, clear results with effect sizes and intervals, and an honest summary of limits are the deliverables that make a strong portfolio piece.
